headline: Consumers and Homebuilders Lead a Broad Rally as Chips Crater
body_html:
Tuesday's session closed on a constructive note for most of the market, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners 323 to 195 across our 519-name universe. The dominant theme was a decisive rotation away from technology hardware and semiconductors, and into consumer-facing, housing-adjacent, and healthcare names — a pattern consistent with investors seeking shelter ahead of potentially market-moving central-bank commentary expected later in the week.

Consumer stocks paced all sectors with a 2.65% gain, homebuilders followed at 2.45%, and healthcare added 2.14%. Software held modest ground at plus 1.85%. The damage was concentrated in semiconductors, which shed 5.61% as a group — the sharpest sectoral loss of the day — while energy dropped 2.34% and materials slipped 0.64%. Industrials were effectively flat, up just 0.11%.

Repligen was the session's standout mover, surging 10.9% to lead all gainers in the life-science tools space. At the other extreme, Amkor Technology collapsed 24.74%, dragging the broader semiconductor complex lower and underscoring just how unforgiving this market remains for chipmakers caught in an earnings crossfire.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Wreckage Deepens on Multiple Fronts
briefs.body: Amkor Technology plunged 24.74%, Sandisk shed 14.25%, and Ichor Holdings dropped 13.03% on Tuesday, collectively hammering the semiconductor index by 5.61%. The synchronized selloff suggests earnings-driven disappointment is spreading across packaging, memory, and equipment sub-segments simultaneously, with no obvious floor yet in sight.

briefs.headline: Sherwin-Williams Paints a Bright Picture for Housing-Linked Names
briefs.body: Shares of Sherwin-Williams rallied 8.24% on Tuesday, a move that complemented a 2.45% advance in the homebuilders sector. The paint-and-coatings giant's surge points to improving sentiment around residential construction activity, offering one of the cleaner read-throughs to housing demand seen in recent sessions.

briefs.headline: Corning Slides as Boeing Diverges — Two Industrial Stories, One Day
briefs.body: Corning tumbled 12.08% Tuesday, landing among the session's worst performers, even as reporting noted that Boeing was moving in the opposite direction. The contrast highlights how idiosyncratic earnings and operational narratives are driving sharp divergences within what is often treated as a monolithic industrial cohort.

briefs.headline: Gold Firms as West Asia Tensions Ease Temporarily
briefs.body: Bullion edged higher in Tuesday trading as a pause in West Asia hostilities reduced the most acute inflation-risk premium in the market. Traders appear to be recalibrating positioning cautiously, unwilling to abandon the metal entirely given continued uncertainty around Federal Reserve policy and the trajectory of geopolitical flashpoints.

briefs.headline: Fed Chair Watch: Markets Parsing Every Word Before Key Appearance
briefs.body: Prediction-market traders were actively pricing scenarios around what Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh may signal in remarks expected this week, with sentiment shifting between rate-path keywords. The anticipation is adding a layer of caution to positioning, particularly in rate-sensitive sectors where valuations hinge on the near-term policy outlook.

briefs.headline: Incyte Jumps as Pharma-Biotech Catches a Bid
briefs.body: Incyte advanced 9.3% on Tuesday, making it the second-largest gainer across the entire universe and a standout within the pharma-biotech space. The move contributed to healthcare's 2.14% sector gain and reinforced a session-wide pattern of investors gravitating toward life-science names as semiconductor exposure became increasingly costly.
